name: Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Ltd
about: Apollo Hospitals was established in 1983 by Dr. Prathap C Reddy, renowned architect of modern healthcare in India. As the nation’s first corporate hospital, Apollo Hospitals is acclaimed for pioneering the private healthcare revolution in the country. Apollo Hospitals has emerged as Asia’s foremost integrated healthcare services provider and has a robust presence across the healthcare ecosystem, including Hospitals, Pharmacies, Primary Care & Diagnostic Clinics and several Retail Health models. [1]

statements.text: Revenue compounded 19.0% a year over 5 years (FY21→FY26); profit after tax 71.0%.
EBITDA margin expanded 420 bps over 5 years (10.8% → 15.0%).
Revenue growth accelerated from 17% to 23% YoY over the last 4 quarters.
Over 5 years: ₹6,395 cr of profit, ₹9,985 cr of operating cash — conversion 1.56x.

During the quarter, we operationalized 75 beds in our Pune facility. As we enter the next fiscal, we will be commissioning four new hospitals, one each in Hyderabad, Kolkata, Bangalore and Gurgaon, further strengthening our presence in key metropolitan markets with strong fundamentals. These facilities, along with the ramp-up in our recently commissioned Pune hospital, will approximately add 1,500 additional operating beds to our network, representing a significant step-up in capacity and a clear runway for medium-term growth.

We expect to operationalize roughly half of this capacity in the upcoming fiscal year with the balance coming online early FY '28. This phased commissioning approach allows us to calibrate ramp-up efficiently, optimize capital deployment and drive occupancy-led operating leverage as demand scales. Together, these additions position us well to capture growth opportunities in high-acuity care, deepen our market penetration and enhance long-term shareholder value.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Revenue growth of ~28% in FY26 and ~30% in FY27 on management's adjusted basis (G12, G13, C2).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Reported consolidated growth was 15.2% in FY26 and 20.9% in H1 FY27, and the 3-year revenue CAGR is 14.9%. The adjusted series is never shown.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: New hospitals will bring ~INR150 crore of ramp-up losses (G4, C1).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: The operating margin rose four quarters running (14.9%, 15.3%, 15.5%, 15.6%), and Q2 FY27 PAT grew 33.6% YoY. Either the losses are smaller than guided or the openings are later than planned; the inputs can't tell which.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Phased commissioning will 'optimize capital deployment and drive occupancy-led operating leverage' (C5).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: 5-year CFO/PAT is 1.56 and 5-year FCF INR3,388 crore. 3-year PAT CAGR of 33.4% against revenue CAGR of 14.9%, with the margin up 260bps, shows operating leverage so far. Working capital has loosened, with CCC moving from -16 to 3 days.

bull.point: Operating leverage is visible: the margin rose four straight quarters to 15.6% (+70bps YoY), and Q2 FY27 PAT grew 33.6% on revenue growth of 23.0%.
Cash backs the profits: 5-year CFO/PAT is 1.56, 5-year FCF INR3,388 crore, and D/E 0.77.

Capacity runway: about 1,500 beds across Pune, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Bangalore and Gurgaon, ~750 of them in FY27, with breakeven targeted within two years. Revenue growth accelerated from 17.2% to 23.0% over four quarters.

bear.point: Growth guidance misses on reported numbers: ~28% was guided for FY26 against 15.2% delivered, and ~30% for FY27 against 20.9% in H1. The guide rests on adjustments (GST cut, Amazon exit) that management chooses.
Execution slipped before FY27 started: environmental delays pushed Gurgaon 2-3 months to Q2 FY27, and the new beds carry ~INR150 crore of guided ramp-up losses, with breakeven two years out.

The digital business is not growing overall: GMV was roughly flat at Q3 FY26 against a ~30% FY26 GMV guide, with growth only in online pharmacy (+32%). ROCE is 17%, with INR8,149 crore of borrowings ahead of the bed build.

questions: Which of Hyderabad, Kolkata, Bangalore and Gurugram are operating today, and how many of the 750 FY27 beds are live?
What were FY26 and H1 FY27 growth on the adjusted basis behind the 28% and 30% guides, and what exactly is excluded? Please reconcile to the reported 15.2% and 20.9%.
How much of the ~INR150 crore ramp-up loss is in H1 FY27, given margins rose to 15.6%, and is the INR25,000 crore run-rate target consolidated or for one business?
